raw_response:
# C21 — catalogue baseline B

I found four useful references. The C++ wording has evidence before the 2014-07-30 cutoff; ATS and D remain undated here, and the retrieved Nim edition is later evidence. These are design-transfer suggestions, not claims of deployment or proven usefulness.

1. **C++ closure classes, copy/reference capture, and mutable invocation.** [N2859](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2009/n2859.pdf), dated 2009-03-19, separates capture choice from a const or mutable inline call operator. It could inform capture policy and environment access while retaining concrete callable types. Reference capture still requires valid lifetimes; this wording does not establish consuming invocation, and inline does not guarantee inlining. Discovered through [Awesome Modern C++](https://github.com/rigtorp/awesome-modern-cpp/blob/master/README.md) and its C++11 FAQ link.

2. **ATS typed closures and linear closure ownership.** [Linear closures](https://ats-lang.sourceforge.net/DOCUMENT/INT2PROGINATS/HTML/x3534.html) and [environment-free versus closure-functions](https://ats-lang.sourceforge.net/DOCUMENT/INT2PROGINATS/HTML/x746.html) distinguish representations and track a closure through reusable calls and explicit destruction. They could inform ownership-controlled environment lifetime and avoiding allocation for local calls. Linear ownership alone is not a consuming-call rule. The book's incomplete copyright range does not date these chapters reliably. Discovered through the [low-level language catalogue](https://github.com/robertmuth/awesome-low-level-programming-languages).

3. **D delegates with escape-sensitive environment storage.** The [D specification](https://dlang.org/spec/function.html) describes shared access to captured locals, context-plus-function delegates, and heap lifetime extension with scope-based allocation avoidance. It could inform a common callable interface serving local and escaping uses. GC-backed capture needs adaptation to an ownership-based language, and the inspected specification has no established cutoff-era edition. Discovered through the [low-level language catalogue](https://github.com/robertmuth/awesome-low-level-programming-languages).

4. **Nim closure procedure values and explicit inline/closure iterator forms.** The [manual](https://nim-lang.org/docs/manual.html) provides an environment-passing representation and a visible optimization-versus-first-class-value choice. This could inform representation and optimization controls; ordinary captures are by reference, and iterator rules do not directly provide consuming/read-only/mutable callable modes. This is later evidence: manual version 2.4.2, [announced 2026-11-13](https://nim-lang.org/blog.html). Discovered through the [low-level language catalogue](https://github.com/robertmuth/awesome-low-level-programming-languages).

Together these suggest examining capture policy, access capability, lifetime, and callable representation separately. I did not establish a complete prior design satisfying every requirement.
